findings.location: Example3 rewritten area integral and sine term
findings.observation: After correctly obtaining 2a²∫cos²θ, the source omits a² in ∫(1+cos2θ)dθ; it restores a² in the split integrals but again omits it from the sine antiderivative and endpoint sine difference.
findings.independent_derivation: The zero sine boundary term makes the finalπa² correct despite these invalid intermediate equalities. Scaling radius a must scale every area term by a².

findings.observation: θ=arctan(y/x) is not a general inverse conversion. r=sqrt(x²+y²) also selects nonnegative r, despite earlier signed-r freedom.
findings.resolution: Choose r≥0 and determineθ with quadrant-aware atan2(y,x), modulo2π; at the originθ is arbitrary. For x<0 adjust the principal arctangent byπ; handle x=0 separately.
findings.independent_derivation: Point(−1,1) has principal arctan(y/x)=−π/4, which with r=sqrt2 reconstructs(1,−1), the wrong point. The same incomplete angle formula recurs in exam review PDF4/printed3.

findings.observation: Distance r describes the r≥0 convention; signed r reverses the ray. Angle intervals with both endpoints included duplicate one direction, and all angles represent the origin.
findings.resolution: Use radians. Assume a>0 for the stated circle radius. Include at least one endpoint±π/2 to include the origin in the circle trace; open interval misses that single point.
findings.independent_derivation: (r,θ) and(−r,θ+π) give identical Cartesian coordinates. Factoring r(r−2a cosθ)=0 does not permit division at r=0, but r=2a cosθ includes the origin atθ=±π/2. The alternative interval shifted byπ traces the same circle because Cartesian x=a(1+cos2θ),y=a sin2θ.

findings.observation: The formula needs the specified radial region and a tracing interval without multiplicity; the infinitesimal triangle argument does not give an explicit limit bound.
findings.resolution: For continuous nonnegative f on an angular interval of length≤2π, use radial region0≤r≤f(θ) and integrate1/2 f². For signed radii or loops, choose intervals and check overlap; r² alone cannot prevent repeated area.
findings.independent_derivation: On each angular subinterval exact sectors with radii min f and max f bound its area by(1/2)min(f)²Δθ and(1/2)max(f)²Δθ. Uniform continuity makes the sums converge to the same integral. The exam handout explicitly warns about missing/double-counted regions.

findings.observation: Both conic equation and four-petal sketch are correct.
findings.resolution: The ellipse is x²/(4/3)+(y+2/3)²/(16/9)=1, with foci(0,0),(0,−4/3). Each rose petal has areaπ/8; all four totalπ/2 if each traced once.
findings.independent_derivation: Ellipse center(0,−2/3), semiaxes4/3 and2/sqrt3 give focal distance2/3. Its y-range[−2,2/3] implies1−y/2>0, so squaring introduces no extra points. The polar denominator is at least1/2. For the first rose petal, (1/2)∫_-π/4^π/4 cos²2θ dθ=π/8; zeros and signs match Figure11.

findings.observation: The source prints ds=sqrt((dx/dt)²+(dy/dt)²), omitting dt. The example immediately below includes dt correctly.
findings.resolution: Write ds=sqrt(x-prime(t)²+y-prime(t)²)dt for increasing t, or ds/dt equal to the speed.
findings.independent_derivation: For x=t^4,y=1+t the speed is sqrt(16t^6+1), and length on[t0,t1] is its integral with t0≤t1; no interval is specified, so no numerical length follows.

findings.observation: The source writes Ax²+Bx+C=A(x−B/(2A))²+C−B²/(4A), and uses u=sqrtA(x−B/(2A)).
findings.resolution: Both minus signs inside the shifted variable must be plus: A(x+B/(2A))²+C−B²/(4A); u=sqrtA(x+B/(2A)) when A>0.
findings.independent_derivation: Expanding the printed right side gives Ax²−Bx+C. For A=1,B=4,C=13 the correct(x+2)²+9 is already stated in the handout footnote on PDF4.

findings.observation: The source prints a2 x+b2 x instead of a2 x+b2.
findings.resolution: Each numerator must be an arbitrary polynomial of degree<2: ak x+bk.
findings.independent_derivation: The printed second numerator is only a multiple of x and cannot represent an independent constant term, e.g.1/(x²+1)² requires that constant.

findings.observation: The sheet prints−ln(cos x) and ln(sec x+tan x) without absolute values or interval restrictions.
findings.resolution: Use−ln|cos x|+C and ln|sec x+tan x|+C on any interval avoiding poles; the printed forms hold where their logarithm arguments are positive.
findings.independent_derivation: At x=π, tan and sec are defined but both printed logarithm arguments are negative. Differentiating the absolute-value forms gives tan and sec wherever cos x≠0.

findings.observation: Arc/surface formulas presuppose suitable piecewise C1 curves and positive orientation of integration. Surface radii are printed as y or x, not absolute values.
findings.resolution: Use nonnegative distance to axis:2π|y|ds or2π|x|ds; for the displayed versions restrict y≥0 or x≥0. Trace a curve once if geometric length/area rather than multiplicity is intended.
findings.independent_derivation: A curve below the x-axis still produces positive surface area; literal2πy ds would be negative. General parameter speed is sqrt(x-prime²+y-prime²). The coordinate forms use increasing x or y, or absolute differentials.

findings.location: Three trig substitutions and derivative formulas
findings.observation: Derivatives and identities are correct, but root simplifications require chosen real branches and a>0.
findings.resolution: For sqrt(a²−x²), use x=a sin u with u∈[−π/2,π/2]; for sqrt(a²+x²), use x=a tan u with that open range; for sqrt(x²−a²), treat x≥a and x≤−a on separate branches and retain absolute values when needed.
findings.independent_derivation: sqrt(a²cos²u)=a|cos u|, sqrt(a²sec²u)=a|sec u|, sqrt(a²tan²u)=a|tan u|. Arcsin derivative needs |x|<1; tan/sec derivatives require cos x≠0 and radians.

findings.observation: Q must be nonzero as a polynomial; antiderivatives are taken on intervals avoiding its real zeros. The real square-root normalization assumes A>0 and an irreducible quadratic with C−B²/(4A)>0.
findings.resolution: Normalize the leading coefficient sign first, then complete the square; reducible quadratics belong to real linear factors. In polynomial division the quotient degree n−m assertion assumes n≥m and nonzero leading coefficients.
findings.independent_derivation: For irreducible real quadratic with A>0, discriminant B²−4AC<0 gives k²=C−B²/(4A)>0. Then u du/(u²+k²)^n reduces by w=u²+k², while du/(u²+k²)^n uses u=k tanθ. These conditions make the stated reduction valid.

findings.observation: The cover-up values B=1,C=1/3 are correct; A is left for the reader. The long division example is correct.
findings.independent_derivation: At x=0,1/2=−A+1+1/6, so A=2/3; multiplying by(x−1)²(x+2) verifies the numerator. Also(x+2)(x²−2x+1)+(3x−2)=x³, and3x−2=3(x−1)+1. Differentiation checks all displayed simple-piece antiderivatives.

findings.observation: The displayed identity is correct; regularity is implicit.
findings.resolution: A sufficient condition is u,v continuously differentiable on[a,b].
findings.independent_derivation: Integrate(uv)-prime=u-prime v+uv-prime and rearrange. The heuristic of choosing the simpler derivative is a strategy, not a guarantee of elementary integrability.

technical_disposition: Both required PDFs are fully covered. Main polar results are correct but the inverse-angle shortcut is incomplete and the circle-area working drops a² factors. The review sheet has missing dt, a wrong completing-square sign, and an extra x in a numerator. Conditions for radii, logarithms, inverse trigonometric branches, arc/surface formulas and rational decomposition are separated from true typos.
unresolved_limits: The parametric arclength example supplies no parameter interval, so a numerical length cannot be determined from this packet.
The source uses open intervals for some closed traces; omitted boundary points have zero area but matter if claiming the entire curve as a set.
